title: Textures inside the Mesh Editor (P6, decision 48): the helper's messages and the Mesh Editor tab's hooks, one contract for both sides

capabilities.texture_paint_v1: the helper takes texture_paint_arm and texture_paint_disarm, sends paint_stroke, and takes texture_paint_refused (this contract). Both sides send these events only when the other announced the capability in hello, so the existing rule that an unknown event is fatal stays as it is, on both sides and in the tab's event whitelist
capabilities.resident_texture_region_updates_v1: the helper applies texture_region_update in place and acknowledges it (the existing ResidentTextureRegionUpdateQueue wire shape, host_to_helper); today the helper treats the event as unknown and fatal (cdmw_session.rs, the unknown-event arm), so this capability is new on the Rust side

about: The Python side is built and tested on refs/heads/rr/parity-p6-python: cdmw/services/model_textures.py (the list, its grouping, the sharing rule and Make unique), cdmw/domain/textures/original_output.py with TextureEditorNativeDdsService.export_matching_original (output in the original's format, colour space and mips, or a refusal with the reason), cdmw/services/texture_document_authority.py (one document per edited texture; the mesh session's store is derived from it), cdmw/services/mesh_draft_textures.py (the draft's texture projects) and the optional pressure in apply_texture_editor_stroke and TextureEditorToolSettings. Tests: tests/test_model_textures.py, tests/test_texture_original_output.py, tests/test_texture_document_authority.py, tests/test_mesh_draft_textures.py, tests/test_texture_editor_stroke_pressure.py, tests/test_build_mod_new_texture_registration.py. The main thread builds what this file lists under 'helper_to_host', 'host_to_helper' and 'tab_hooks'; nothing here is wired into cdmw/ui/mesh_editor, cdmw/ui/preview or tools/rust_mesh_lab yet. Every envelope field (protocol, session_id, process_generation) is as in every other helper message.

units.uv: the part's texture coordinates as the PAC stores them, u right and v down in the texture's pixel space after the same V convention the helper already uses to sample the base texture; (0, 0) is the texture's top-left texel corner, (1, 1) the bottom-right
units.pressure: 0.0 to 1.0; a pointer without pressure leaves the field out of every sample (never sends 1.0 for 'unknown')
units.rect: x, y, width, height in texels of the full-resolution texture document

helper_to_host.when: only while the brush is armed (texture_paint_arm), on the part under the pointer; one 'begin', any number of 'samples', one 'end' (or 'cancel') per stroke

fields.stroke_id: integer, increasing per helper process; every message of one stroke carries the same id
fields.part: integer, the scene submesh index under the pointer at 'begin' (the stroke stays on this part)
fields.resource_id: string, the texture resource the panel chose (as in the manifest's textures rows)
fields.channel: string, the host's channel name copied from texture_paint_arm (see 'channels')
fields.samples: array of {u, v, pressure?}, in order; at most limits.samples_per_message per message (a longer one is refused with invalid_arguments); empty for 'end' and 'cancel'
fields.base_revision: integer, the helper's shadow revision, as transaction_request carries it
fields.role: string, the helper's role for that channel (see 'channels')

helper_to_host.host_answer: none per message; the visible result is texture_region_update, and a refusal is texture_paint_refused

helper_to_host.host_handling: ResidentTextureRegionUpdateQueue.acknowledge (cdmw/ui/mesh_editor/resident_texture_update_queue.py); a failed update is retried once, then the host sends the whole texture again

fields.resource_id: string, the texture the panel chose
fields.parts: array of scene submesh indices the brush may paint (the parts whose material reads the texture)

host_to_helper.helper_handling: the pointer paints instead of selecting while armed; a stroke outside 'parts' is not sent
the pointer selects again; a stroke in progress ends with 'cancel'

fields.message: the sentence the editor's status line shows

host_to_helper.helper_handling: the stroke's live marks are dropped and the message is shown

host_to_helper.shape: exactly what ResidentTextureRegionUpdateQueue builds today: schema 'cdmw_resident_texture_region_update_v1', version 1, session_id, edit_revision, texture_revision, generation, resource_id, channel, affected_submeshes, texture_width, texture_height, rect {x, y, width, height}, pixel_format 'bgra8_unorm', row_pitch, binary {path, offset, length, sha256, delete_after}
host_to_helper.helper_handling: upload the rectangle into the resident GPU texture for (resource_id, channel) and acknowledge with texture_region_applied; a texture shown downscaled (the 2048 px preview cap) takes the rectangle scaled into its own resolution; nothing reinstalls the document
host_to_helper.one_writer_rule: the authority is the only writer of the mesh session's texture store. The tab builds each ResidentTextureRegionRequest with mesh_service=None, so the queue writes nothing itself, and with document_texture_revision set to the revision TextureDocumentAuthority.commit returned (M1 of the review)
host_to_helper.limits: a region larger than limits.region_bytes is sent as tiles of at most that size, each its own update; the first update of a texture above 4096x4096 is therefore tiled too. A failed update is retried once by the queue; after a second failure the host sends the whole texture again as tiles. The host enforces all three, not the helper

tab_hooks.when: a Mesh Editor session opens on an archive model (after MeshArchiveMaterialContextWorker has the preview model)
tab_hooks.call: model_textures.model_texture_list_from_preview(the preview model's meshes): it stamps each mesh's part on its slot rows (the app's slot producers set no part_name; H1 of the review)
tab_hooks.result: groups in panel order: colour, normal, material_response, masks, detail, emissive, other (TEXTURE_GROUPS); labels are the UI's: Colour, Normal, Material response, Masks, Detail and layer, Emissive, Other

tab_hooks.when: the user chooses a texture to edit
tab_hooks.call: original_output.check_texture_editable(the extracted DDS path), before the editor opens it
tab_hooks.refusal: TextureOutputRefused.reason is the message; the texture is not opened

tab_hooks.when: after the check, before the first stroke
tab_hooks.call: model_textures.texture_sharing(texture, parts being edited, other_files=<the archive scan's users or None>, own_files=<this model's own files>)
tab_hooks.result: TextureSharing: needs_unique (shared: offer Make unique), in_place (known to be read only by the parts being edited: the edit may write the texture's own path) and reason. An in-place edit happens only when in_place is true; until the on-request scan has run (other_files None) or when a part is unnamed, the panel offers 'Check other files' or Make unique and the reason says why (H2 of the review)

tab_hooks.call: model_textures.make_texture_unique(source_path, sidecar_path=, sidecar_data=<the session's current sidecar bytes>, parts=, stem=<the model's stem>, existing_paths=<game and mod paths, any spelling>, owner=<the draft's id>)
tab_hooks.result: MadeUnique: the session's replacement companions gain the rewritten sidecar (sidecar_path, sidecar_data) and, at Build Mod, the edited texture at new_path; the shared original is never written. Registration needs no host code: DMM and CDMW's virtual loader register a mod's new DDS files (tests/test_build_mod_new_texture_registration.py)

tab_hooks.when: the editor opens the texture (docked or the app's Texture Editor)
tab_hooks.call: TextureDocumentAuthority.open(TextureDocumentKey.of(session_id, resource_id, channel), document, layer_pixels, owner=<'Mesh Editor' or 'Texture Editor'>, affected_submeshes=, logical_path=); keep the returned entry's token: commit, reload_from_store, adopt and close take it
tab_hooks.refusal: TextureDocumentOpenElsewhere: focus the widget named by .owner instead of opening a second copy; the same label is not enough, only the token reopens (M3 of the review)

tab_hooks.call: map each sample's UV to texels with the document's size, then apply_texture_editor_stroke(document, layer_pixels, tool_settings, points, pressures=<the samples' pressures, or None when the pointer sent none>), then TextureDocumentAuthority.commit(key, document, layer_pixels, token=) (the authority measures what changed; M5), then queue texture_region_update for that rect
tab_hooks.notes: samples may be applied as they arrive for live feedback; commit runs once per stroke so a stroke is one history step
tab_hooks.refusal: TextureDocumentStale (a mesh Undo or another writer changed the store): reload_from_store, rebuild the document from it, adopt, then apply the stroke again (M2 of the review)

tab_hooks.when: Finish (each Finish is one restorable step, decision 38)
tab_hooks.call: mesh_draft_textures.save_draft_texture(<the draft folder: mesh_layer_project_path's parent>, DraftTexture(resource_id, channel, source_path, output_path=<source_path or MadeUnique.new_path>, parts, affected_submeshes, original_format, sidecar_path, source_sha256, source_width, source_height, finish_generation), document, layer_pixels)
mesh_draft_textures.load_draft_textures(draft folder), then for each loaded texture TextureDocumentAuthority.open and commit (whole texture) so the mesh store matches the saved document
tab_hooks.refusal: a LoadedDraftTexture with problem set is shown by name and not reopened; the rest of the draft opens; before reopening, mesh_draft_textures.source_changed(texture, <the game's current DDS>, width=, height=) says when a game update replaced the source (M8), and that texture is not reopened

tab_hooks.when: Build Mod, and the archive result that sends users to it
tab_hooks.call: for each edited texture: TextureEditorNativeDdsService.export_matching_original(document, layer_pixels, original_texture_output(parse_dds(original)), <staging path>) and add the DDS at DraftTexture.output_path as a replacement companion
tab_hooks.lift: the mesh-only refusal at cdmw/workers/mesh_editor_workers.py ('Mesh-only outputs cannot contain texture or material authoring changes', in MeshDirectOutputWorker.run) and at cdmw/services/mesh_archive_results.py is lifted when every committed texture resource has a draft texture with an output; Export Mesh File keeps its refusal and says 'Export Mesh File writes the mesh only; use Build Mod to include texture edits.'; hair is lifted too, since its output already copies, renames and registers textures (decision 48)

refusal_codes.not_editable: check_texture_editable refused: the format cannot be written back unchanged (TextureOutputRefused.reason)
refusal_codes.needs_unique: the texture is shared (texture_sharing.reason) and Make unique was not accepted
refusal_codes.open_elsewhere: TextureDocumentOpenElsewhere: the document is open in another widget
refusal_codes.stale_revision: TextureDocumentStale: the mesh store changed under the document; it is reloaded
refusal_codes.no_texture: the part under the pointer has no texture in the chosen channel
refusal_codes.source_changed: the game's copy of the texture changed since the edit was saved
refusal_codes.too_many_samples: a paint_stroke message carried more than limits.samples_per_message samples

channels.about: The host names channels as the mesh session's texture store does; the helper names roles as its manifest does (_TEXTURE_RESOURCE_SPECS in cdmw/services/mesh_rust_authoring.py). Every message of this contract carries the host's channel name in 'channel' and the helper's role in 'role'.
channels.no_role: material_mask and detail_mask have no role in the helper's manifest: they are edited in the docked editor and written at Finish, with no live paint on the model and no texture_region_update
